title: Anagram Check
prompt: A word puzzle needs to know whether two words use the same letters. Write a function that returns true when the two lowercase strings are anagrams of each other, otherwise false.

explanation.beginner:
Example: anagramCheck("listen", "silent") produces true. Compare letter multiplicities, not just which letters appear. Sorting both character sequences produces the same canonical order for anagrams.

Compare “rejects different letters”: input ["apple","apply"] produces false. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Compare letter multiplicities, not just which letters appear. Sorting both character sequences produces the same canonical order for anagrams.

Tempting mistake: A Set loses duplicate counts: aab and abb contain the same distinct letters but are not anagrams.

The reference uses sort, join. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost. Sorting costs O(n log n + m log m) time and O(n + m) copied characters. A frequency table can reduce the time to O(n + m).

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “rejects different letters”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
